title: The Lookalike List Playbook: 500 Companies Like Your Best Customer
description: Start from your 5 best customers and build a list of companies that look exactly like them. Steps, tools and the outreach sequence.
lead: This is the Lookalike List Playbook from the reel. Start from your 5 best customers and build a list of companies that look just like them.
insider: Targeting is where we spend most of our setup time. A well-built list is how one client got **4,372 replies and 1,061 interested leads in one quarter**. Tools make lookalike lists fast. Cleaning them, finding the right people and verifying every email is the part most teams skip, and the part we handle for clients.

blocks.text: One rep (an AE at Ocean, shared on HeyReach's site) started from her top 5 customers and got **173 requests and 41 meetings**.

items: Pick 5 customers you'd love to clone: happy, paying and easy to work with.
Feed them into a lookalike tool, like Ocean.io, to find similar companies.
Cut anything that doesn't fit: wrong size, wrong country, wrong business model.
Find 2 to 3 decision makers per company.
Use the customer they look like as your proof: "We help companies like [customer]."
Her sequence: connect on LinkedIn with no note, then a voice note, then a short video.

blocks.text: Describe your best customer with Claude

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text:
Here are my 5 best customers (name, website, what they buy from me):
[paste]

Find what they have in common: industry, company size, location, tech they use, how they sell, recent changes (hiring, funding, new locations). Then write the filters I should use in a lookalike or lead database tool, and 3 job titles I should target at each company.

blocks.label: Warning
blocks.text: It only works if your 5 really are your best. Five average customers give you 500 average leads.

faq.q: I don't have 5 customers yet. What now?
faq.a: Use the 1 to 3 you have, or describe the customer you want in detail and build filters from that.
Both work. The rep in this example used LinkedIn. We often run both together.
